football_evidence.question: Can Massachusetts contain Ball State’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 0.5 points.

When Ball State has the ball (big plays on the ground): Ball State’s offense turns 3.7% of its runs into explosive gains, and Massachusetts’ defense gives up explosive gains on 3.9% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Massachusetts’ secondary No. 41 nationally and Ball State’s No. 124.

contradicting: When Ball State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Ball State’s offense has allowed a sack on 4.9% of its dropbacks, and Massachusetts’ defense sacks the quarterback on 2.3% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Ball State has the ball (the red zone): Ball State’s offense succeeds on 57.5% of its red-zone plays, and Massachusetts’ defense allows success on 38.1% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.5%).

Keldric Luster has completed 134 of 211 passes (63.5%) for 1,359 yards, 6.4 yards per attempt, 9 touchdowns and 6 interceptions in seven games for Ball State, and has been sacked on 11 of 222 dropbacks.
Tyler Mizzell has completed 24 of 39 passes (61.5%) for 270 yards, 6.9 yards per attempt, 1 touchdown and no interceptions in five games for Ball State, and has been sacked on 2 of 41 dropbacks.
